author: Codex assessment agent /root/liberal_conservative (AI-assisted doctrinal interpretation)
changeNote: Completed 240 independently considered answers to the current bank from the scoped doctrine. No imported 12Axes vectors or score targets. User authorised neutral answers and completion on 2026-10-04. Conditional modern applications and mixed-causation modelling are explicitly inferred, not claims of direct statements or scientific findings. Independent review completed on 2026-10-04; question-meaning and evidence corrections are recorded in review notes.

metadata.name: Neoconservatism (post-Cold War American school)
metadata.description: The post-Cold War American neoconservative school associated with the Project for the New American Century: American primacy and democracy promotion, distinguished from nationalist non-interventionism.
metadata.scope: The post-Cold War American neoconservative school associated with the Project for the New American Century: American primacy and democracy promotion, distinguished from nationalist non-interventionism. This is a representative interpretation of the specified doctrine, not answers personally submitted by every adherent. Modern technological questions apply the doctrine conditionally. Trait-specific neutral responses express a stated mixed-causation model where the doctrine rejects a single fixed causal priority; they are not empirical scientific estimates.
metadata.phrase: A society with market institutions and established civic values, protected by military strength and an active international role.

sources.title: Why Neoconservatism Still Matters (Brookings Policy Paper 20, May 2010; exact day not given in linked edition)
Strategy and the Idea of Freedom by Douglas J. Feith

axes.brief: The post-Cold War school promotes liberal democracy and strong elected leadership.
axes.counterEvidence: Elite intellectual origins do not imply expert government; foreign alliances with imperfect regimes qualify universalist rhetoric.

answers.rationale: Competitive elections are central to the democratic order defended abroad.
Expert leadership cannot replace democratic legitimacy.
Modern liberal democracy accepts equal adult political standing.
Strong executive leadership must retain constitutional authority.
Genuine democracy requires opposition electoral competition.
Representative scrutiny sustains legitimate national leadership.
Constitutional restraints distinguish liberal democracy from tyranny.
Union appointment is not government by the whole electorate.
Incumbent ideological exclusions contradict competitive democracy.
Popular participation and constitutional representative judgment both matter.
Strategic leadership does not abolish institutional checks.
Defined removal is compatible with constitutional democratic resilience.
A leader cannot suspend elections solely for continuity.
Recall may deter abuse but can weaken stable representative responsibility.
Unaccountable power contradicts democracy promotion's stated premise.
Military coups cannot substitute for legitimate civilian rule.

axes.brief: National security and public order qualify liberal civil liberties.
axes.counterEvidence: This model does not import every Bush administration practice; unlimited detention is not automatically neoconservative doctrine.

answers.rationale: Social order and criticism of permissive counterculture limit drug autonomy.
Lawful surveillance is a necessary national-security instrument.
Political demonstration is legitimate but obstruction can impair public order.
Political argument is part of the liberal order being defended.
Protective responsibility and individual freedom need case-specific balance.
Security utility competes with constitutional privacy limits.
Preventive road-safety checks fit ordered liberty.
Judicially established dangerousness can justify temporary restriction.
Expression rights compete with concern about corrosive mass culture.
Anonymous communication and security identification have competing claims.
Credible serious violence supports proportionate preventive policing.
Likely serious disorder can justify restriction under law.
The rule of law requires independent protection of private homes.
Disclosure must balance accountability and operational national security.
American constitutional self-defence rights remain legitimate with checks.
Persistent executive detention without judicial review exceeds ordered liberty.

axes.brief: Civic patriotism and assimilation are favoured over separatist identity politics.
axes.counterEvidence: Universal democratic aspirations and rejection of racial nationalism permit multiple private cultural identities.

answers.rationale: Shared civic culture sustains national democratic cohesion.
Access accommodation is reasonable without institutionalising separate civic orders.
Newcomers should participate in established national civic customs.
Private heritage can survive within American political identification.
A shared public language supports participation and solidarity.
Historical recognition is compatible with patriotism unless made separatist.
Common national traditions deserve significant cultural support.
Group priorities should not supersede common citizenship.
Shared civic routines encourage integration across communities.
Diverse heritage is accepted within a unifying civic identity.
Integration counters the separatism criticised by this school.
Practical language help must serve eventual common participation.
Shared national allegiance should integrate particular attachments.
Religious freedom and general security rules require reconciliation.
Civic nationalism can accommodate distinct private ways of life.
Integration should teach shared institutions and common customs.

axes.brief: Civic assimilation and national security coexist with openness to people joining democratic society.
axes.counterEvidence: The school is not equivalent to later nationalist mass-restriction programmes; modern visa answers are qualified inferences.

answers.rationale: Admission capacity matters without a doctrinal fixed numerical ceiling.
Joining a free society is a legitimate aspiration.
Family and humanitarian routes qualify skills-only selection.
Family unity can assist stable civic integration.
Protection against tyranny supports refugee admission with security vetting.
Lawful administration weighs against a general right to remain illegally.
Economic demand and civic integration capacity must both count.
Service pressures may justify temporary restraint, not categorical closure.
Family unity and coherent intake planning need balance.
Productive work supports successful entry and integration.
Sponsorship can help without being universally necessary.

Domestic study supports integration and a possible graduate route, while security and durable civic attachment can favour separate qualifying criteria. These competing considerations do not determine a categorical rule about a degree-based route.
Fleeing persecution merits an exception to ordinary limits.
Civic allegiance is more relevant than inherited cultural origin.
Basic inclusion is legitimate while welfare eligibility can require attachment.
Plurality is acceptable, but cultural difference is not the admission objective.

axes.brief: American primacy, democracy promotion and military readiness favour forceful global engagement.
axes.counterEvidence: Brookings distinguishes the school from realism and isolationism, and notes disagreement over particular wars.

answers.rationale: Force can protect the democratic international order before direct attack.
Diplomacy is useful but cannot invariably displace timely coercion.
Maintaining overwhelming capability is central to primacy.
Preventing well-evidenced imminent attack fits proactive defence.
Defence of order and democracy extends beyond responding to attacks.
Service obligations compete with preference for highly capable professional forces.
Major concessions risk rewarding aggression and undermining deterrence.
Military technological advantage favours development with reliability safeguards.
Global security requires more than homeland attack repulsion.
Abandoning attacked allies contradicts democratic solidarity and credibility.
Sustained expeditionary capability is essential to global leadership.

A territorial claim alone gives a weak reason for war, while this school can prioritise enforcing a strategically important settlement through force. The conditional response concerns initiating force, not simply responding to an invasion.
Credible coercive threats are legitimate instruments against hostile powers.
Demonstrated resolve can outweigh immediate de-escalation preferences.
Strategic intelligence is integral to maintaining superiority.
Arms reductions are suspect where they erode primacy or deterrence.

axes.brief: Active international engagement is combined with resistance to supranational constraints on American action.
axes.counterEvidence: Internationalism here means engagement, not automatically pooled legal sovereignty under this quiz's definition.

answers.rationale: American constitutional institutions retain ultimate authority.
International organisations should not veto necessary American action.
Domestic constitutional authority can override conflicting external rulings.
Enduring democratic alliances support the international order.
Sovereign withdrawal remains available when commitments obstruct security.
External jurisdiction over national officials can obstruct legitimate action.
National interests and democratic leadership outrank organisational preference.
Environmental cooperation is useful without unlimited delegated authority.
A compulsory common foreign policy can unduly constrain leadership.
Rights promotion is supported while binding external authority is contested.
Independent monetary sovereignty supports national strategic capacity.
Joint resources can strengthen coalitions and international order.
National institutions should retain decisive admission authority.
Negotiated trade rules support the open democratic order.
National leadership does not require joining political federation.
Defending common democratic order can outweigh immediate material gain.

axes.brief: Market-oriented democratic capitalism coexists with an accepted welfare state and public strategic functions.
axes.counterEvidence: The earlier domestic school opposed utopian social engineering, not every public service or social programme.

answers.rationale: Private enterprise is the normal economic foundation.
Utility ownership is pragmatic where monopoly and security arise.
Comparable performance generally favours private initiative.
Routine public competition with firms lacks a general justification.
Plural competitive providers can supply publicly supported care.
Infrastructure ownership depends on effectiveness rather than a fixed creed.
Competitive contracting is reasonable if public obligations survive.
A public bank needs an identifiable strategic or social function.
Competitive commercial assets can generally be privatised.
Housing support is accepted without requiring extensive direct ownership.
Strong regulation can preserve private strategic firms.
Private resource development normally fits market-oriented capitalism.
Routine services can use competitive providers.
Strategic value may justify retention despite sale opportunities.
Commercial discipline favours restructuring or sale of persistently failing firms.
Public broadcasting can serve civic purposes but requires independence.

axes.brief: An open international economic order supports American leadership, with strategic exceptions.
axes.counterEvidence: Security concerns qualify free trade without turning the doctrine into tariff-centred nationalism.

answers.rationale: General producer protection weakens the open economic order.
Lower barriers support prosperity and ties among democratic societies.
Defence procurement can justify domestic preference beyond ordinary purchases.
Businesses normally benefit from flexible international sourcing.
Essential defence supply may require preserving domestic capacity.
Unilateral openness depends on strategic and reciprocal consequences.
Industrial infancy alone is weaker than a concrete security rationale.
Foreign investment is generally welcome subject to security screening.
Food resilience matters without an unlimited farm-protection principle.
Competitive adjustment normally improves economic strength.
Retaliation can defend fair rules but also weaken allies.
Origin-neutral taxation generally fits open markets.
Foreign state distortion can warrant targeted countermeasures.
Liberalising agreements are favoured unless dependencies endanger security.
Hostile control of strategic firms threatens national power.
Ordinary international digital commerce should remain open.

axes.brief: Markets provide prosperity, with national strategy and welfare institutions correcting selected failures.
axes.counterEvidence: Confidence in foreign nation-building must not be confused with comprehensive domestic economic planning.

answers.rationale: Ordinary output decisions belong to private enterprise.
Compulsory production targets are incompatible with normal market allocation.
Competitive prices generally allocate resources better than administration.
Defence investment is strategic; economy-wide direction is not required.
Consumer demand should normally govern commercial viability.
Price caps risk shortages and inefficient incentives.
Open entry sustains innovation and competitive strength.
Routine politically directed credit invites inefficient favouritism.
Capital movement is normally free subject to security limits.
Strategic support may be justified without general industrial steering.
Monetary experimentation must coexist with systemic stability.
A wage floor's effects on work and opportunity require practical evaluation.
Negotiation is preferable to government wage schedules.
Monetary credibility should not be subordinated to production plans.
Supply-oriented housing markets generally outweigh broad price controls.
Central production coordination is not the doctrine's domestic economic model.

axes.brief: A functioning welfare state is accepted while extensive equalisation and social-engineering ambitions are questioned.
axes.counterEvidence: This differs from minarchism: social insurance and targeted assistance remain legitimate.

answers.rationale: Large income compression risks damaging incentives and social institutions.
Income difference alone does not prove an injustice requiring taxation.
Income security and work incentives require balanced provision.
A practical safety net is preferred to extensive outcome levelling.
Progression may be useful without punitive rates or absolute equality.
Rewarding productive earnings supports growth and responsibility.
Inheritance taxation balances opportunity against family continuity.
Work-oriented conditions can justify time-limited support with safeguards.
Broad wealth transfers can produce adverse institutional incentives.
Fiscal restraint must not eliminate an effective welfare floor.
A stable democratic society needs meaningful inclusion, not bare survival.
Growth-oriented tax relief is generally preferred to broad benefit expansion.
In-work supplements can reward responsibility while relieving hardship.
Tax design is judged by incentives and financing needs rather than one rate rule.
Land redistribution risks disrupting secure property and productive institutions.
Targeting need is useful, but prevention and social insurance justify broader coverage.

axes.brief: Religion is valued as a source of civic morality within American constitutional pluralism.
axes.counterEvidence: Jewish, Christian and secular adherents cannot be collapsed into a single state religion.

answers.rationale: Civil legislation needs reasons beyond one particular revelation.
Religious moral influence differs from an official scripture code.
Elected government does not depend on clerical permission.
Religious heritage matters while constitutional pluralism rejects exclusive establishment.
Common schools may explain faith traditions without compelled adherence.
State conversion-oriented teaching threatens plural citizenship.
Civil law governs enforceable judgments.
Religious consultation does not imply official legislative authority.
Public ceremonial religion can sustain civic tradition.
Religious community activity and direct belief promotion need distinction.
Inherited symbolism may be compatible with plural civic belonging.
Major religious holidays support continuity and shared public culture.
Religious office does not confer political representation.
Religious institutional independence can support exemptions.
Civil marriage should be legally available without clerical permission.
Separate binding religious jurisdiction risks unequal civil protection.

axes.brief: Family stability, civic virtue and criticism of counterculture favour moderate traditionalism.
axes.counterEvidence: The school includes secular and socially liberal adherents; not every contemporary culture-war position follows.

answers.rationale: Adaptation is legitimate when it sustains rather than dissolves civic institutions.
Inherited practices deserve weight against rapid cultural experimentation.
Household dignity coexists with emphasis on stable married families.
Family roles may be valued without rigidly assigning every occupation.
Civil equality and traditional marriage commitments divide this tendency.
Stable married two-parent families are treated as socially valuable.
Personal autonomy and concern for unborn life remain in tension.
Parents have substantial responsibility for children's moral upbringing.
Child welfare and family tradition yield conditional judgments.
Public modesty supports a restrained civic culture.
Respectful accommodation need not entail every contested language convention.
Moral transmission is important for the stability of democratic capitalism.
Individual freedom coexists with the value placed on conventional roles.
Incremental change helps preserve social trust.
Understanding diversity must be balanced with age and parental responsibilities.
Historical continuity carries value beyond immediate utility.

axes.brief: Technological leadership supports economic and military primacy; bioethical risk deserves separate scrutiny.
axes.counterEvidence: Defence innovation cannot establish a position on every invasive consumer or reproductive technology.

answers.rationale: Useful innovation strengthens national capability and prosperity.
Trial duration should reflect specific risks rather than general resistance.
Major public infrastructure may justify proportionate habitat trade-offs.
Medical safety protects citizens and institutional confidence.
Productivity-enhancing AI supports competitive national strength.
Essential development should not face an absolute preservation veto.
Food-system innovation requires practical assessment of safety and benefit.
Permanent enhancement warrants stronger evidence than ordinary technology.
Technological capability offers an important route to environmental security.
Environmental investigation is necessary but indefinite delay can be costly.
Adult choice competes with durable risk and human-dignity concerns.
Reliable diagnosis is essential before routine deployment.
Heritable enhancement raises moral risks beyond ordinary innovation.
Agricultural capacity and ecological resilience need case-specific balancing.
Infrastructure investment supports national vitality with proportionate safeguards.
Irreversible damage warrants caution despite general technological optimism.

axes.brief: American constitutional federalism coexists with strong national security and civic institutions.
axes.counterEvidence: The school is not defined by either comprehensive decentralisation or unitary administration.

answers.rationale: Protected state competence is part of constitutional democracy.
Courts and constitutional allocation should settle competence disputes.
National cohesion cannot be dissolved by unilateral regional preference.
Legitimate nationwide security and civic programmes can override obstruction.
State constitutions are acceptable within common national rights.
National security coordination need not abolish local police accountability.
Local fiscal responsibility coexists with shared national obligations.
Civic educational standards can coexist with state curricular discretion.
State taxation can reflect local democratic choices.
Common labour protections and experimentation deserve balance.
Local boundaries may involve wider constitutional and administrative interests.
National coverage commitments can coexist with regional variation.
Distinct institutions must respect individual rights and national citizenship.
Fiscal competition is useful until it undermines common capacity.
Purely regional effects favour regionally accountable administration.
Multi-region threats require effective national coordination.

axes.brief: Scepticism about unlimited social engineering coexists with civic education and universal democratic capacities.
axes.counterEvidence: Human imperfection is not genetic determinism; trait-specific causal rankings remain mixed interpretive judgments.

answers.rationale: Social formation matters while stable human dispositions constrain reform.

International IQ comparisons involve education, health, measurement and inheritance; the scoped doctrine does not assign a stable causal priority. This representative response adopts a mixed model rather than inferring biology from citizenship or tradition.
Sex differences can involve socialisation and embodied differences.
Stress sensitivity involves constitution and experience without doctrinal priority.
Education and institutional incentives shape interests.
Risk-taking reflects both dispositions and learned incentives.
Cooperation depends importantly on civic and family institutions.
Empathy draws on human capacities and social cultivation.
Attention differences cannot be reduced to the school's critique of social engineering.
Moral intuitions involve predisposition and transmitted civic norms.
Political education and historical experience shape perceived threats.
Temperamental variation interacts with social development.
Attraction preferences combine bodily and cultural influences.

Violence rates can reflect social conditions, institutions and individual dispositions; the doctrine supplies no defensible racial causal ranking. The representative model therefore withholds primacy rather than deriving empirical claims from equal rights.
Family discipline and institutions explain learned self-control better than racial destiny.
Individual choices, incentives and unequal social expectations can all affect pay.

review.reviewer: Codex independent assessment reviewer /root/socialist_green (separate from author)
review.notes: Independently read all 240 answers against the current bank and checked the scoped primary doctrine plus scholarship/context. No scores or desired locations were consulted. Reviewed literal government authority, ownership versus funding, official religious review versus veto, graduate routes versus guaranteed residence, military initiation versus response, and causal claims versus moral equality. Corrections: restricted-immigration-open-immigration-12: 0 -> 0; militarist-pacifist-12: 0 -> 0. The inferred modern-policy answers and mixed causal models remain representative applications, not documented answers by every adherent or scientific causal estimates. Similarity review is a subsequent mechanical check. Brookings explicitly distinguishes the later foreign-policy school from the earlier domestic school; domestic answers are cautious representative extensions and more weakly specified than the five foreign-policy tenets. Corrected the linked Brookings edition date: May 2010 without an exact day. Validation returned zero errors. Explicitly examined neutral-count warnings: authority-liberty 6/16, assimilation-multiculturalism 5/16, restricted-immigration-open-immigration 8/16, public-private 6/16, high-redistribution-low-redistribution 6/16, progressive-traditionalist 9/16, innovation-caution 5/16, central-local 9/16, culture-nature 12/16. Retained condition-dependent policy tradeoffs and representative interaction models; in particular the Culture vs Nature neutrals withhold causal primacy rather than converting equal rights into empirical proof. High neutrality records weaker doctrinal determination and must not be presented as a precisely measured consensus among adherents. No answers were changed after inspecting validation scores.
